description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Danish Gambit. Decline with 3...d5! or take and strike back in the center.

drills.briefExplanation: 2...exd4 3.c3 d5! 4.exd5 Qxd5 — take, block, trade, and centralize the queen.
drills.description: Black to play. White offers the Danish with 2.d4 — take and decline the second pawn.
drills.explanation: The safest antidote to the Danish: after 2...exd4 3.c3, Black plays 3...d5! — declining the second pawn. After 4.exd5 Qxd5 Black is a pawn up with a centralized queen and a solid structure; White's gambit idea (open lines for the bishops) fizzles against the closed center. Sometimes the best tactic is refusing the gift.
drills.name: Declining the Second Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: 4...cxb2! 5.Bxb2 d5! — accept both pawns, then strike in the center.
drills.description: Black to play. White offered the second pawn with 4.Bc4 — take it, then strike with 5...d5!.
drills.explanation: The brave defense: after 4.Bc4 Black takes the second pawn with 4...cxb2!, then plays 5...d5! before White consolidates. The central strike challenges White's bishops and says: the pawns are mine, and the initiative too. White's compensation evaporates if Black develops quickly — greed works when followed by energy.
drills.name: Take and Strike
